title: Scalar compatibility of normalized finite smooth orientations at divisible exponents
statement: Let A and B be finite commutative rings with a unital map φ:A→B. Let N,M>0, M dividing N, N A=0 and M B=0. Let X,Y be Noetherian schemes and f:X→Y a separated quasi-compact compactifiable smooth map of pure dimension d. Assume N invertible on X and Y and M invertible on X. Supply the coefficient-independent closed-diagonal Geometry witness [lem-trf-finite-ring-section-deformation]. Let α_A:ω_(f,A)≅A_X(d)[2d] at exponent N and α_B:ω_(f,B)≅B_X(d)[2d] at exponent M have OrientationNormalized witnesses, meaning the diagonal-factor, normalized Rees-specialization and normal-bundle integration equations of [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps]. Let t be a CoefficientLineComparison, with the N/M root power and its generator and derived-counit normalizations [def-pur-finite-smooth-coefficient-arrows]. Then Q_X(α_A.inv) ≫ dualizingScalarMap φ f = (t.tensorPower d).hom ≫ α_B.inv. The exceptional scalar map is the specified unit-normalized mate of [def-pur-exceptional-coefficient-tensor-maps].

proof.text: Unpack the two OrientationNormalized witnesses as κ, normalized at one, the Cartesian cone-to-bundle squares, and the defining equations. normalSectionMap_isIso and bundleAdjoint_isIso make their final composite invertible. Cancel that composite and apply integratedSpecialization_normalization to write α_A.hom = diagonalFactor_A ≫ ψ_A and α_B.hom = diagonalFactor_B ≫ ψ_B.

Mapping N A=0 along φ gives N B=0. Apply finiteSmoothDiagonalScalar at the common annihilator N, and integratedSpecialization_scalar at N,M with the supplied normalized κ maps, cone squares and t. Functor.map_comp and associativity paste their two squares, giving c_f ≫ α_B.hom = Q_X(α_A.hom) ≫ (t.tensorPower d).hom.

Postcompose the desired inverse equation with α_B.hom, an isomorphism. Substitute the forward equation, use functoriality to combine Q_X(α_A.inv) and Q_X(α_A.hom), and cancel both inverse-hom composites. This establishes precisely the displayed equation without needing invertibility of the exceptional coefficient mate.

lean.statement:
theorem normalizedOrientation_scalar
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (N M : ℕ) (hN : 0 < N) (hM : 0 < M) (hMN : M ∣ N)
    (hA : (N : A) = 0) (hB : (M : B) = 0)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (hY : IsUnit (N : Γ(Y, ⊤))) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [HasCompactification f] [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f]
    (geometry : FiniteRingSectionDeformation.Geometry d
      (pullback.fst f f) (pullback.diagonal f))
    (hX : IsUnit (N : Γ(X, ⊤))) (hX' : IsUnit (M : Γ(X, ⊤)))
    (alphaN : dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f ≅ line A N hA X d)
    (alphaM : dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) f ≅ line B M hB X d)
    (_hn : OrientationNormalized A N hN hA f d geometry hX alphaN)
    (_hm : OrientationNormalized B M hM hB f d geometry hX' alphaM)
    (t : CoefficientLineComparison φ N M hA hB X) :
    (ordinaryScalar φ X).map alphaN.inv ≫ ExceptionalCoefficients.dualizingScalarMap φ f =
      (t.tensorPower d).hom ≫ alphaM.inv
